native_region: Endemic to the southern Eastern Ghats mountain range in Andhra Pradesh, India
ecological_importance: Endemic cornerstone species of dry deciduous thorn and scrub forests. Supports specialized insect pollinators and contributes organic matter to rocky, nutrient-poor soils.
threats: Rampant international smuggling and illegal harvesting for high-value heartwood
field_identification_notes: Trifoliolate leathery leaves with rounded to ovate leaflets.
Dark, rugged, blocky bark exuding blood-red resin (pterocarpin) when injured.
ml_relevance: Trifoliolate leaves and dark blocky bark with red exudate.

ar_information.quick_identification: Trifoliolate leathery leaves; dark blocky bark bleeding red resin; circular winged pods.
ar_information.ecological_importance: Keystone endemic of dry scrub forests.
ar_information.conservation_message: Endangered (EN) CITES Appendix II. Highly prized globally for its rich red heartwood, making it one of the most heavily trafficked timber species in the world.
